labels.message: Function `Program` calls `RegExpParser` with a loop-invariant pattern.
labels.reason: The parser is rebuilt with identical options on every iteration; it could be created once.

checks.reason: The pattern handed to RegExpParser is `regexContent`, the content of the individual regex literal being processed, so it is not a loop-invariant operand that can be cached.

labels.message: Function `_parse` calls `RegExp` with a loop-invariant pattern.
labels.reason: The RegExp is already lazily cached behind `if (!emojiRegex)`; nothing is recompiled per iteration.

checks.reason: `new RegExp(_emojiRegex, "u")` is already guarded by `if (!emojiRegex)`, i.e. a lazy first-use cache, so it is not recompiled on each call.

The `if (!emojiRegex)` guard already caches the regex, so `new RegExp(...)` at line 816 runs at most once and the 'compiled repeatedly' claim fails; this is the lazy-init idiom the rule should recognize.
